name: Continuity — character-locked, live-paced
description: Presentation shell for single-character POV videos rendered sequentially via img2img. Defines HOW the video is built: you drop in a character sheet, the planner picks an establishing scene, and every following scene references the previous render (and/or the sheet) so the on-screen character stays consistent. Pacing is audio-driven — you set a per-episode min/max scene length and the planner cuts more often where the narration is busy. Pipeline: idea → first-person script → audio → per-chapter subtitles → stitched timeline → Character Sheet → Scene Plan (paced cuts) → sequential Continuity Render → Scene Review → Timestamp Video Assembly. The niche layered on top sets the voice and subject. SLOW by design (each scene waits on the previous render) in exchange for character consistency. NOT for evenly-distributed scene-images (use Scenes), NOT for stock footage (use Stock Footage).

idea.systemPromptRole: You are helping generate first-person, point-of-view episode ideas for a creator-led channel where ONE consistent on-screen character carries the whole video. Each idea should lend itself to a sequence of concrete, visualizable moments the character physically moves through. The niche layered on top (if any) sets the subject domain and voice.
idea.guidanceText: Each idea should imply a clear sequence of scenes the character physically moves through, so the continuity chain has distinct beats to render. Keep it first-person and concrete — abstract topics give the planner nothing to render.

script.systemPromptRole: You are writing a point-of-view narration where ONE character carries the whole video and the visuals are rendered scene-by-scene to match the audio. Give the visual planner clear, concrete physical beats to latch onto — what the on-screen character is doing, holding, looking at, or where they are — because each beat becomes its own rendered scene in a continuity chain. Short, vivid, action-anchored sentences beat long abstract ones. The niche layer sets voice and subject.
additionalRules: Keep the chosen point of view (the Point-of-view setting) consistent throughout.
Anchor each idea to a concrete, visualizable action or location — the planner turns these into scenes.
Prefer short, punchy sentences over long abstract ones; busy passages should imply faster cuts.
Keep one consistent on-screen persona — don't introduce new unnamed people the chain can't render consistently.
pacingArc: Setup: the starting situation, shown as an establishing scene
Core: the step-by-step body, each step its own concrete beat
Momentum: a busier stretch of quick actions (faster cuts)
Payoff: the result, tie back to the opening premise
script.closingHint: End on the payoff that resolves the opening premise.

narratorStyles.label: Casual first-person
narratorStyles.description: Relaxed, conversational 'talking to a friend' voice. The default for POV creator content.

narratorStyles.label: High-energy
narratorStyles.description: Faster, punchier, motivational — leans into momentum and quick wins.

narratorStyles.label: Calm and deliberate
narratorStyles.description: Measured, confident, 'let me walk you through this' pacing. Good for thoughtful walkthroughs.

imagePrompts.purposeNote: (populated by the Scene Plan page — the LLM produces one visual prompt per planned scene, paced to the user-set min/max scene length. The Continuity Render then generates each scene sequentially, anchoring on the character sheet and optionally referencing the previous scene's render.)
imagePrompts.visualStyleHint: Keep the SAME character, wardrobe, and setting consistent across every scene — the continuity chain depends on it. Describe what the character is doing in this beat; the look is carried by the reference images.
imagePrompts.defaultStyleTag: Consistent character, consistent lighting and style across scenes. Cohesive, grounded, slightly cinematic. The same person should be recognizable in every frame.

thumbnail.conceptGuidance: A cover featuring the recurring character as a clear hero, mid-action in a relatable setting, in the same consistent look used across the chain. The viewer should recognize the character instantly.
compositionRules: Recurring character as the clear hero, large in frame, mid-action
Consistent wardrobe and style with the rest of the chain
Relatable, grounded setting with a clean area for the title
